content.title: About
content.content: NFS Cookie is a sweet baked product made from flour, sugar, butter and various add‑ins such as chocolate, nuts or raisins. It features a crisp edge and a soft, aromatic interior. The snack is popular as a quick bite and is often served with tea or coffee.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Mass production of cookies began in the 19th century in the United States.
There are more than 400 varieties of cookies, ranging from simple sugar cookies to complex spiced recipes.
Cookies are frequently used as a base for no‑bake desserts like cheesecake crusts.
In many cultures cookies are a traditional gift for holidays.
The term “home‑baked cookie” denotes products made without industrial additives.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Carbohydrates provide a quick boost of energy, making cookies a convenient snack.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Small amounts of B1 and B2 support carbohydrate metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: When whole‑grain flour or nuts are used, cookies can contribute to digestive health.

items.title: Antioxidants from add‑ins
items.content: Chocolate, dried fruit or nuts add antioxidant compounds.

items.title: Mood improvement
items.content: Sugar triggers serotonin release, which can temporarily lift mood.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Excessive consumption may lead to weight gain and increase the risk of cavities.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Cookies often contain nuts, gluten and dairy, which can cause allergic reactions.

items.title: Trans‑fat content
items.content: Some commercial recipes use partially hydrogenated oils, which are harmful to heart health.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Cookies can cause rapid blood‑sugar spikes, problematic for people with diabetes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cookies can be enjoyed on their own, paired with tea, coffee or milk, or incorporated into desserts such as layered cakes or ice‑cream mixes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cookies in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life, keep them in the refrigerator to prevent fat oxidation.
